residency.test: Citizens and green card holders are taxed on worldwide income regardless of where they live. Others are resident under the substantial presence test.
residency.substantial_presence: 31 days in the current year AND 183 days counting current year + 1/3 of prior year + 1/6 of the year before that.
residency.worldwide_income: Yes - the US is one of only two countries taxing citizens on worldwide income wherever they reside.
residency.exit: Expatriation may trigger the section 877A exit tax for covered expatriates.

headline.payroll: 7.65% employee FICA up to the Social Security wage base, plus 0.9% additional Medicare on high wages
headline.state_tax: 0% to ~13.3% depending on state; nine states levy no tax on wage income
headline.capital_gains: 0/15/20% long-term, plus 3.8% net investment income tax above 200,000 / 250,000

standard_deduction.name: Standard deduction
standard_deduction.note: 2025 amounts as increased by the July 2025 reconciliation act

employee.name: Additional Medicare
employee.note: threshold is 250,000 for married filing jointly

credits.note: phase-out starts at 400,000 for joint filers; up to 1,700 per child is refundable

local_tax.name: State income tax
local_tax.note: state tax varies enormously; pass --region or --local-rate

CA.name: California
CA.note: approximate high-bracket rate; California is progressive to 13.3%

WA.note: no wage income tax; 7% tax on large long-term capital gains

capital_gains.long_term: 0% / 15% / 20% depending on total taxable income; holding period over one year
capital_gains.principal_residence: up to 250,000 (single) / 500,000 (joint) of gain excluded if owned and used 2 of the last 5 years

quirks: Citizens and green card holders must file from abroad. The foreign earned income exclusion (130,000 for 2025) and foreign tax credit usually eliminate double tax, but the return is still due.

FBAR (FinCEN 114) is separate from the tax return and is triggered by aggregate foreign account balances over 10,000 at any point in the year. Penalties are severe and unrelated to whether tax was owed.
State residency is decided separately from federal residency, and some states (notably California and New York) are aggressive about domicile after a move.
Estimated tax payments are due quarterly for income without withholding; underpayment penalties accrue even if the return is filed on time.
The alternative minimum tax still applies to some taxpayers with large deductions or incentive stock option exercises.

reporting.who_must_file: Anyone with gross income above the standard deduction for their status, plus anyone with net self-employment income of 400 or more, regardless of total income.

deadlines.what: Form 1040 filing and payment deadline for tax year 2025
Automatic deadline for citizens living abroad
deadlines.note: filing extension only - interest still runs from 15 April

deadlines.what: Extended deadline if Form 4868 was filed

forms.name: Profit or loss from business (sole proprietors)
Statement of specified foreign financial assets (FATCA)
Report of foreign bank and financial accounts (FBAR)

documents_to_collect: Form 1095-A if health coverage came from the marketplace
Records of estimated tax payments already made

penalties.late_filing: 5% of unpaid tax per month, capped at 25%
penalties.late_payment: 0.5% of unpaid tax per month, capped at 25%
penalties.accuracy: 20% of the underpayment for substantial understatement or negligence
penalties.fbar: up to 10,000 per non-wilful violation; wilful violations far higher

warnings: State and city income taxes are approximated by a single rate. For California, New York City, Oregon and other progressive-state cases, compute state tax separately.
The alternative minimum tax, net investment income tax and qualified business income deduction are not modelled.
